extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent agents, patent litigants, inventors, and USPTO practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory standards and procedural rules from 35 U.S.C. (and associated editor notes) governing patent infringement remedies, post‑grant procedures (reexamination/inter partes review applicability), false marking, invention promotion, joinder, state liability, and related patent‑process requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 288: Action for infringement of a patent containing an invalid claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a claim of a patent is invalid, an action may be maintained for the infringement of a claim of the patent which may be valid. The patentee shall recover no costs unless a disclaimer of the invalid claim has been entered at the Patent and Trademark Office before the commencement of the suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to proceedings commenced on or after Sept. 16, 2012 (editor note refers to AIA applicability); amended 1975 and 2011. The pre‑AIA variant (see separate entry) uses the phrase 'without deceptive intention.'

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 288 (pre‑AIA) variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, without deceptive intention, a claim of a patent is invalid, an action may be maintained for the infringement of a claim of the patent which may be valid. The patentee shall recover no costs unless a disclaimer of the invalid claim has been entered at the Patent and Trademark Office before the commencement of the suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical/pre‑AIA wording emphasizing 'without deceptive intention'; editor notes indicate applicability distinctions based on filing dates and AIA transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 289: Remedy for design patent infringement (profits remedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever during the term of a patent for a design, without license of the owner, applies the patented design (or colorable imitation) to any article of manufacture for the purpose of sale, or sells/exposes for sale such article, shall be liable to the owner to the extent of his total profit, but not less than $250, recoverable in any U.S. district court having jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not prevent other remedies; prevents double recovery of the profit made from the infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 290: Notice of patent suits (clerk reporting duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerks of U.S. courts, within one month after filing an action under this title, shall give notice in writing to the Director, setting forth so far as known the names and addresses of the parties, name of the inventor, and the patent number. If other patents are included later or after decision/judgment, similar notices must be given; the Director shall enter such notices in the file of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to filings and to later additions/decisions; amendment history cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 291: Relief for owner of a patent derived by another (derived patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a patent may have relief by civil action against the owner of another patent that claims the same invention and has an earlier effective filing date, if the invention claimed in such other patent was derived from the inventor of the invention claimed in the patent owned by the person seeking relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing limitation: action must be filed only before the end of the 1‑year period beginning on the date of issuance of the first patent containing a claim to the allegedly derived invention and naming an individual alleged to have derived such invention as inventor or joint inventor. Editor notes specify applicability to AIA first‑to‑file transitional provisions and effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 291 (pre‑AIA): Interfering patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of an interfering patent may have relief against the owner of another by civil action, and the court may adjudge the question of validity of any of the interfering patents, in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre‑AIA provisions referenced for patents not subject to first‑inventor‑to‑file rules; procedural cross‑references to section 146.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 292: False marking prohibitions and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits marking or using in advertising the name or imitation of the patentee, patent number, or words like 'patent' with intent of counterfeiting or deceiving the public, or marking unpatented articles with words like 'patent' or 'patent applied for' when no application exists or is not pending, for the purpose of deceiving the public. Violation is a fine not more than $500 for each offense (only the United States may sue for that penalty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private parties: a person who has suffered competitive injury may file a civil action for damages adequate to compensate. Marking a product with matter relating to an expired patent is not a violation. Subsection amendments and effective dates noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 293: Nonresident patentee; designation for service and jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patentee not residing in the United States may file in the PTO a written designation naming a person residing within the U.S. upon whom process or notice of proceedings affecting the patent may be served. If no such designation or the designee cannot be found, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia shall have jurisdiction and may direct service by publication or otherwise; the court has the same jurisdiction as if the patentee were personally within it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment history provided; establishes practical service mechanism and jurisdiction for nonresident patentees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 294: Voluntary arbitration of patent disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract involving a patent may contain a provision requiring arbitration of any dispute relating to patent validity or infringement arising under the contract; absent such provision, parties to an existing dispute may agree in writing to arbitrate. Such provisions/agreements are valid, irrevocable, and enforceable except on grounds for revocation of contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arbitration governed by Title 9 to the extent not inconsistent with this section; defenses under section 282 shall be considered by the arbitrator if raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 295: Presumption for products made by patented processes
rubrics_metrics.description: In actions alleging infringement of a process patent based on importation, sale, offer for sale, or use of a product made from a process patented in the U.S., if the court finds (1) that a substantial likelihood exists that the product was made by the patented process, and (2) that the plaintiff made a reasonable effort to determine the process actually used and was unable to determine, the product shall be presumed to have been so made; the burden of establishing that the product was not made by the process shall be on the party asserting that it was not so made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumption applies in process‑based infringement cases involving products; added Aug. 23, 1988; amendment history cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 296: States and instrumentalities not immune from patent suit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State, any instrumentality of a State, and any officer or employee of a State or instrumentality of a State, acting in official capacity, shall not be immune under the Eleventh Amendment or other sovereign immunity doctrine from suit in Federal court by any person for infringement of a patent under section 271, or any other violation under this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies in such suits include those available against private entities: damages, interest, costs, treble damages under section 284, attorney fees under section 285, and design patent remedial provisions under section 289.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 297: Duty and disclosure requirements for invention promoters
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention promoter must disclose in writing, prior to entering into a contract for invention promotion services, specified information including: (1) total number of inventions evaluated in past 5 years and number with positive/negative evaluations; (2) total number of customers in past 5 years (with exclusions); (3) total number of customers known to have received a net financial profit as direct result of services; (4) total number known to have received license agreements as direct result; (5) names and addresses of all previous invention promotion companies with which promoter or officers were affiliated in previous 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil remedies: customers injured by material false/fraudulent statements or omissions may recover actual damages or statutory damages up to $5,000 (customer may elect). If court finds willful misrepresentation aimed to deceive, damages may be increased up to three times, considering past complaints/regulatory sanctions compiled by the Commissioner. Definitions provided for 'contract for invention promotion services', 'customer', 'invention promoter', and 'invention promotion services'. Commissioner must make complaints publicly available after providing promoter opportunity to reply and may solicit complaints from other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 298: Advice of counsel evidence rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure of an infringer to obtain the advice of counsel with respect to any allegedly infringed patent, or the failure to present such advice to the court or jury, may not be used to prove that the accused infringer willfully infringed the patent or that the infringer intended to induce infringement of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added Sept. 16, 2011; effective as to patents issued on or after Sept. 16, 2012 and applicable to civil actions commenced on or after Jan. 14, 2013 as adjusted by later legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 299: Joinder limits for accused infringers
rubrics_metrics.description: Accused infringers may be joined in one action as defendants or counterclaim defendants, or have their actions consolidated for trial, only if (1) any right to relief is asserted against the parties jointly, severally, or alternatively with respect to or arising out of the same transaction, occurrence, or series of transactions relating to the making/using/importing/offering/selling of the same accused product or process; and (2) questions of fact common to all defendants will arise in the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accused infringers may not be joined solely on allegations that each has infringed the patent(s) in suit. A party that is an accused infringer may waive these limitations. Section applies to civil actions arising under any Act of Congress relating to patents, with the exception noted for §271(e)(2) actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 301: Citation of prior art and written statements to the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time may cite to the Office in writing prior art consisting of patents or printed publications believed to bear on the patentability of any claim, or statements of the patent owner filed in proceedings where the owner took a position on claim scope. If the person explains the pertinence and manner of applying the prior art or statements to at least one claim, the citation and explanation shall become part of the official file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written statements must include other documents/pleadings from the proceeding that address the statement. Limitations: such written statements/additional information are to be considered by the Office only to determine proper meaning of a patent claim in proceedings ordered under sections 304, 314, or 324. If subject to protective order, redactions are required. Upon written request, the identity of the person citing may be kept confidential in the patent file.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 302: Request for reexamination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time may file a request for reexamination by the Office of any claim of a patent on the basis of any prior art cited under §301. The request must be in writing, accompanied by payment of a reexamination fee, and must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested. Unless the requester is the patent owner, the Director will promptly send a copy of the request to the owner of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee amount established by the Director under section 41. Procedural mailing to patent owner required if requester is not owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 303: Director's determination on reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months following filing of a request for reexamination under §302, the Director will determine whether a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim is raised by the request, with or without consideration of other patents or publications. The Director may on his own initiative determine whether a substantial new question is raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A record of the Director's determination will be placed in the official file and a copy mailed to owner and requester. A determination that no substantial new question has been raised is final and nonappealable; upon such a determination the Director may refund a portion of the reexamination fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 304: Reexamination order and patent owner statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director finds a substantial new question of patentability under §303(a), the determination will include an order for reexamination. The patent owner will be given a reasonable period, not less than two months from the date of the determination being mailed/given, to file a statement including any amendment to the patent and new claim(s) proposed for consideration in the reexamination. If the owner files such a statement, he must promptly serve a copy on the person who requested reexamination. Within two months of service, the requester may file and have considered a reply to any statement filed by the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures opportunity for owner and requester to present statements/amendments; sets minimum reply periods and service obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 305: Conduct of reexamination proceedings (current AIA‑applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the times for filing the statement and reply under §304 have expired, reexamination will be conducted according to procedures established for initial examination under §§132 and 133. In reexamination, the patent owner may propose any amendment to the patent and new claim(s) to distinguish the claimed invention from prior art cited under §301 or in response to an adverse decision. No proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim will be permitted. All reexamination proceedings, including appeals to the PTAB, will be conducted with special dispatch within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor note: Applicable to patents issuing from applications subject to first‑inventor‑to‑file provisions of the AIA; pre‑AIA variant exists. Cross‑references to examination procedures §§132–133 and appeal routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 305 (pre‑AIA) conduct provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If Director finds a substantial new question of patentability, order for reexamination includes similar opportunities for owner to file statements and propose amendments/new claims to distinguish from cited prior art; no proposed amendment/new claim enlarging scope permitted; proceedings (including appeals to Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences) will be conducted with special dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older procedural references (Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences) are retained for patents/applications not subject to AIA first‑to‑file; editorial notes clarify applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 306: Appeal rights in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner involved in a reexamination proceeding may appeal under the provisions of section 134, and may seek court review under the provisions of sections 141 to 144 with respect to any decision adverse to the patentability of any original or proposed amended or new claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the administrative and judicial appeal routes for adverse reexamination decisions; amendment history cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 307: Certificate of patentability, unpatentability, and claim cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: In a reexamination proceeding, when appeal time has expired or appeals have terminated, the Director will issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined to be unpatentable, confirming any claim determined to be patentable, and incorporating into the patent any proposed amended or new claim determined to be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposed amended/new claim incorporated into a patent following reexamination has the same effect as specified in §252 for reissued patents regarding rights of prior users or those who made/purchased/used/imported items covered by such claim or made substantial preparation prior to the issuance of the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 311 (note): Inter partes review applicability (AIA transition rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post‑grant review provisions of the AIA apply only to proceedings commenced on or after Sept. 16, 2012, with certain transitional and grandfathering rules (e.g., extension of jurisdiction of Federal Circuit to certain appeals is deemed to take effect Sept. 16, 2011; pre‑AIA provisions continue to apply to inter partes reexaminations requested before Sept. 16, 2012; PTAB may be deemed Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences for certain pre‑AIA matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor notes explain transitional applicability, crossover dates, and how pre‑AIA and AIA procedures interrelate for reexaminations and appeals.
